title: Emergency Cutoff Tripped
shortDescription: The high-temperature safety has tripped due to overheating.
fullDescription:
The ECO (Emergency Cutoff) on Atwood water heaters is a one-shot thermal fuse that opens at about 180°F on the tank. Once tripped, the heater locks out until manually reset.

Causes include a failed thermostat sticking closed, dry operation (no water in tank), or mineral buildup insulating the sensor. Reset the ECO by pressing the red button on the thermostat assembly — but only after addressing the root cause.

Never attempt to operate with the bypass valves in winterize position or the tank empty — heating elements and gas burners burn out quickly.

fixSteps.title: Verify tank full
fixSteps.instruction: Run hot tap until steady stream to confirm water in tank.

fixSteps.title: Reset ECO
fixSteps.instruction: Press the red button at the thermostat/ECO assembly.

fixSteps.title: Test thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If ECO retrips, replace the thermostat/ECO combo.

whenToCallPro: If the tank has been run dry and the element burned — element replacement requires draining.
videoSearchQuery: Atwood RV water heater ECO reset

faq.q: Is it safe to bypass ECO?
faq.a: Absolutely not — it prevents scalding and tank failure.

title: Direct Spark Ignition Lockout
shortDescription: The DSI module attempted ignition three times with no flame and locked out.
fullDescription:
Atwood DSI water heaters spark, open the gas valve, and sense flame rectification. If no flame is detected after three trials, the module locks out and the red LED illuminates.

Common causes: low propane, dirty/spider-webbed burner tube, corroded ground path, worn electrode. Reset by switching off and on at the interior switch.

Do not force multiple retries without diagnosis — raw propane vented without ignition is a flash hazard.

causes.cause: Dirty burner / spider web in venturi
Low propane or closed tank valve

fixSteps.title: Reset switch
fixSteps.instruction: Switch heater off for 30 seconds, then on.

fixSteps.title: Clean burner
fixSteps.instruction: Remove burner tube, blow out with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Check electrode
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for cracks and set gap to 1/8 inch.

fixSteps.title: Verify ground
fixSteps.instruction: Clean ground lug at burner mount.

whenToCallPro: If gas valve or circuit board is suspected — propane work should be verified with leak check.
videoSearchQuery: Atwood DSI water heater lockout fix

faq.a: Insects love the warm, dark burner tube during storage.

title: No Spark At Electrode
shortDescription: The ignition module is not producing spark.
fullDescription:
When the DSI board opens the gas valve but no spark is visible at the electrode, the issue is in the HV path — electrode cracked, HV cable pinched, or module internal failure.

Test by observing spark through the burner access hole with the heater cycling.

High voltage present — do not touch electrode during spark test.

fixSteps.title: Visual inspect electrode
fixSteps.instruction: Look for hairline cracks or carbon tracks.

whenToCallPro: If module replacement needed or gas valve troubleshooting.
videoSearchQuery: Atwood water heater no spark electrode

faq.q: How do I know if my electrode is bad?
faq.a: Visible cracks or lack of spark during retry — replace as a set.

title: Pilot Light Won't Stay Lit (Pilot Models)
shortDescription: Older pilot-light Atwood models drop out the pilot after release.
fullDescription:
Pre-DSI Atwood water heaters used a manual piezo pilot with a thermocouple. When the thermocouple fails or cools too quickly, the pilot drops out on button release.

Clean the thermocouple tip, confirm it's in the pilot flame, and check the magnetic valve. Most failures are thermocouple-related.

Never hold the pilot button more than 60 seconds without ignition — unburned gas accumulates.
symptoms: Pilot lights but dies on release

fixSteps.title: Clean thermocouple
fixSteps.instruction: Remove, polish tip with fine sandpaper, reinstall.

whenToCallPro: If gas valve is suspect — magnetic valve requires soap leak check.
videoSearchQuery: Atwood water heater pilot won't stay lit

faq.q: Do new Atwoods still use pilots?
faq.a: No — all current models are DSI (electronic ignition).

title: Yellow Flame / Burner Combustion Issue
shortDescription: Burner is producing yellow flame and sooting, indicating combustion problems.
fullDescription:
A properly tuned Atwood burner produces a sharp blue flame. Yellow or wavering flame means too little air, too much propane, or a dirty burner — this causes soot buildup in the tube, CO production, and eventual shutdown.

Clean the burner tube, check the orifice for partial blockage, and inspect the air shutter adjustment.

Sooted flue tubes are a fire risk — clean thoroughly before returning to service.

fixSteps.title: Clean burner
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out burner tube with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Adjust air shutter
fixSteps.instruction: Open shutter until flame goes sharp blue.

fixSteps.title: Clean flue
fixSteps.instruction: Brush flue tube free of soot.

whenToCallPro: If CO is detected inside the RV — safety inspection warranted.
videoSearchQuery: Atwood water heater yellow flame fix

faq.a: Yes — above 4500 ft, derate per manual and adjust air shutter.

title: Thermostat Open / Won't Cycle
shortDescription: The operating thermostat is not closing to call for heat.
fullDescription:
Atwood heaters use a combination thermostat/ECO mounted on the outside of the tank. The thermostat closes around 120°F set point. If it fails open, the heater never fires; if it fails closed, the ECO eventually trips.

Test with a multimeter at room temperature — should show continuity.

Always replace thermostat and ECO as a combo — same housing, similar age.

fixSteps.title: Test continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure — open at cold tank = failed.

whenToCallPro: Rarely — this is straightforward DIY for anyone comfortable with basic electrics.

faq.q: How do I know which wire is which?
faq.a: Label before disconnecting — Atwood wiring is not color-keyed universally.

title: AC Heating Element Failure
shortDescription: The 120V electric heating element has burned out or has wiring fault.
fullDescription:
Atwood/Dometic electric-option water heaters use a 1400W screw-in element similar to a household heater. Dry-fire (running without water) burns elements in minutes.

Normal element resistance is ~10 ohms. Open = failed.

Drain the tank before removing the element — boiling-hot water under pressure can cause severe burns.
symptoms: No hot water on electric mode

fixSteps.title: Shut off power and drain
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off AC breaker, close cold supply, open drain plug.

fixSteps.title: Remove element
fixSteps.instruction: Use 1-1/16 inch socket to unthread element.

fixSteps.title: Install new element
fixSteps.instruction: Wrap with Teflon tape, torque to spec, refill tank.

whenToCallPro: If the threads in the tank are damaged — stripped threads mean tank replacement.

faq.q: Can I flush scale off the element?
faq.a: Yes — soak in white vinegar overnight.

title: Gas Valve Not Opening
shortDescription: The solenoid-operated gas valve is not energizing or has mechanical failure.
fullDescription:
Atwood DSI water heaters use a 12V solenoid valve. When the DSI board calls for ignition, it energizes the solenoid. If the valve doesn't audibly click or open, no gas reaches the burner.

Measure 12V at valve coil during a trial. Replace the entire valve as a unit — rebuilding is not recommended on RV appliances.

After replacement, leak-check all joints with soapy water.

fixSteps.title: Measure coil voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 12V at valve coil during trial.

fixSteps.title: Replace gas valve
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off propane, remove and install new valve, leak test.

whenToCallPro: If you lack propane leak-test experience — any leak is a fire hazard.
videoSearchQuery: Atwood water heater gas valve replace

faq.q: Do I have to pull the whole heater?
faq.a: Often yes — the valve is behind the burner assembly.

title: Tank Water Leak
shortDescription: Water dripping from the heater indicates a tank, PRV, or drain plug leak.
fullDescription:
Atwood water heater tanks are aluminum (unlike Suburban's steel tanks) and resistant to electrolysis. Leaks are usually the plastic drain plug, PRV, or tank-to-burner-tube gasket — not the tank itself.

If the aluminum tank does develop a pinhole, replacement is usually cheaper than repair.

Shut off water supply and 120V before disassembly.

fixSteps.title: Tighten drain plug
fixSteps.instruction: Snug the plastic drain with proper socket.

fixSteps.title: Replace PRV
fixSteps.instruction: If PRV leaks after cool-down, install new 150 psi / 210°F PRV.

fixSteps.title: Assess tank
fixSteps.instruction: Any leak from tank body = replace heater.

whenToCallPro: Tank body leak — replacement requires removing heater from RV wall.

faq.q: Do Atwood tanks need an anode rod?
faq.a: No — aluminum tanks don't use anodes, unlike Suburban.

title: Interior On/Off Switch Fault
shortDescription: The interior rocker switch or wiring is not supplying 12V to the heater.
fullDescription:
Atwood water heaters are controlled by a rocker switch inside the RV. If the switch fails, the DSI module never powers up and nothing happens when pressed.

Check for 12V at the switch and downstream at the DSI board. Also check the fuse for the water heater circuit.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Test 12V fuse for water heater circuit.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage across switch terminals in both positions.

whenToCallPro: If harness troubleshooting involves pulling multiple panels.

faq.q: My switch lights up but heater doesn't fire?
faq.a: That's a DSI lockout, not a switch issue — see DSI code.
